subject.title: [Bug]: exec tool silently corrupts 2>&1 / 2>/dev/null shell redirect arguments

question: Should maintainers sponsor a current-main/package repro pass for this exec redirect corruption report before allowing any fix PR?
rationale: The issue has concrete shipped-version examples, but inspected current source and Codex contracts preserve the command string, so the first failing layer is still unknown.

options.title: Reproduce before fix
options.body: Run a focused exec scenario on current main or the latest package and queue implementation only after the mutation boundary is captured.

options.title: Wait for reporter proof
options.body: Keep the issue open but require fresh logs, a screenshot, or a recording before spending maintainer time on a repro lane.

options.title: Close after non-repro proof
options.body: Close only if maintainers can show current main and the latest package preserve `2>&1` without corruption with exact command/argv proof.

recommendation.title: Reproduce before fix
recommendation.body: Run a focused exec scenario on current main or the latest package and queue implementation only after the mutation boundary is captured.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has the strongest history across exec host routing, approval trust, and redirect-adjacent allowlist behavior.
